page: Amazon Web Services m6gd.large is a general-purpose cloud server powered by AWS Graviton2 processors built on the 64-bit ARM Neoverse-N1 architecture. Running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 2 dedicated physical cores (2 vCPUs) clocked at 2.5 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core configuration. Memory allocation totals 8.0 GB of RAM, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Notably, the instance includes an integrated 118 GB NVMe SSD for direct local storage, while GPU acceleration is not present. Network connectivity delivers a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Benchmark evaluations position the m6gd.large in lower-tier performance tiers across overall compute and memory metrics. While stress-ng single-core execution sits in the average band at 1519.39, multi-core operations register in the lower 25% at 3013.17. Synthetic results from Geekbench 6 reflect similar limitations, recording a single-core score of 958.0 and a multi-core score of 1752.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 38.91 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 19.3 GB/sec for writes. Application tests record static web serving throughput of 2.41 GB/sec and Redis SET performance of 2.28 million operations per second, indicating modest throughput under intensive I/O and processing pressure.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 Graviton architecture provides low hardware operating overhead, but the 2-vCPU configuration limits parallel execution. The primary trade-off centers on raw computing capacity versus localized fast storage: high-speed NVMe access provides low-latency disk operations, but compute-heavy tasks face constraints from the 2-core ARM ceiling. As a result, the instance is appropriate for microservices, lightweight web servers, caching nodes, continuous integration workers, and temporary scratch storage workloads where high CPU concurrency is not mandatory.
